The classic Risk world board

Source: R/data.R
risk_map.Rd

The standard 42-territory, 6-continent Risk board: which territories exist, which of them border one another, how they group into continents, the bonus armies each continent is worth, and static coordinates for drawing the board. rk_world() wraps this dataset into an rk_map object.

Usage

risk_map

Format

A list with five elements:

territories

Character vector of the 42 territory names, in board order (North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia).

adjacency

Named list with one element per territory, each a character vector of the territories it borders. The graph is symmetric and no territory borders itself.

continent

Named list with one element per continent, each a character vector of its territories. Every territory belongs to exactly one continent.

continent_bonus

Named integer vector of the extra armies a player receives for holding each continent: North America 5, South America 2, Europe 5, Africa 3, Asia 7, Australia 2.

layout

A tibble::tibble() with 42 rows and columns territory (character), x and y (double plotting coordinates on a 0-100 canvas) and continent (character).

Source

The territory, adjacency and continent structure of the standard Risk board; assembled by data-raw/make_map.R. The plotting coordinates are a schematic layout, not a geographic projection.

See also

Other map: rk_map(), rk_neighbors(), rk_world()

Examples

risk_map$continent_bonus
#> North_America South_America        Europe        Africa          Asia 
#>             5             2             5             3             7 
#>     Australia 
#>             2 
risk_map$adjacency$Brazil
#> [1] "Venezuela"    "Peru"         "Argentina"    "North_Africa"
